recentItems.title: China's First Liquid Immersion Cooling Pod for Computer Servers Put into Operation
recentItems.description:
Scientists in a lab in China's Guizhou Province have started testing different means of cooling data servers, including by submerging them in vats of liquid.

Inside these liquid-cooled immersion pods for computer servers, rigorous compatibility tests are being carried out on four different types of coolants.

Experts say with growing demand for AI computing power, traditional air cooling is no longer effective at managing the heat dissipation needs of high-power chips. Full-immersion liquid cooling has emerged as a solution.

Besides keeping the servers cool, the tanks are also conducting compatibility testing on silicone oil, synthetic oil, reclaimed transformer oil, and fluorinated fluids.

Scientists say, although its performance needs improvement, for now fluorinated fluid has proven to be the most stable means of liquid cooling.

Experts predict that immersion liquid cooling will gradually replace traditional cold-plate liquid cooling systems as the technology advances and costs decrease.

recentItems.title: AI Computing Sparks a Copper Rush in China
recentItems.description:
As AI fuels a growing need for computing hardware, one of the most essential items, copper, is in short supply in China.

In east China's Jiangxi Province, production lines at a copper processing plant are running around the clock to meet demand.

In east China's Anhui Province, meanwhile, this company makes "hyper very low profiles", or HVLP copper foil, which is a major ingredient in printed circuit boards for AI servers.

Experts say the data signaling rate with HVLP copper foil is 70 percent faster than with traditional copper foil.

Data shows that demand for HVLP copper exceeds supplies from Q4 of last year.

The amount of copper needed to meet AI computing demand last year was roughly 28 million tons. By 2040 that number is expected to increase to 42 million tons.
